cards.q: Which two environments have become primary reservoirs of microplastic pollutants?
What is the trade-off of using sludge to enrich soil?
cards.a: It provides nutrients but simultaneously introduces substantial microplastic content.

cards.q: Beyond altering soil properties, what can accumulated microplastics pollute?
Which two soil physical properties do microplastics detrimentally affect?
cards.a: Soil bulk density and aggregate stability.

cards.q: What else does the presence of microplastics alter in soil?
On what do microplastics' effects on sludge properties, microbial communities and soil characteristics depend?
What microplastic concentrations does the review report for sludge versus soil?
cards.a: 271 Particles/kg dry weight in sludge versus 34.6 Particles/kg in soil.

cards.q: What R² value expresses the correlation between microplastic concentrations in soil and sludge?
Which p-value indicates a significant correlation between microplastic amounts in soil and sludge?
Which p-value suggests no significant association between microplastic concentrations in wastewater and sludge?
Which microplastic shapes predominate in sludge and soil?
What is the predominance of fibers and fragments in soil often linked to?
How does microplastic contamination in terrestrial environments compare with that in marine environments?
cards.a: It has risen significantly, far exceeding levels in marine environments.
